items.prompt: Which evidence would most strongly justify reconstructing literary history around contemporary readers rather than later canonical fame?
choices: Readers’ letters, marginalia, and published reviews
Modern sales rankings and bestseller lists
Winners of recent literary prize awards
Texts included in current university syllabi
items.answer: Readers’ letters, marginalia, and published reviews
items.rationale: Contemporary reception records reveal how works were actually read and valued at the time, challenging retrospective canons based on later fame.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: A scholar proposes a period based on changing representations of catastrophe. Which methodological concern is strongest?
choices: The symbolic role of catastrophe may vary among works, so the boundary requires historical justification
Every literary period must begin with a military conflict
Themes may organize literary history only when several countries are compared
A recurring image can never provide evidence of historical change
items.answer: The symbolic role of catastrophe may vary among works, so the boundary requires historical justification
items.rationale: A thematic boundary risks treating unlike works as historically uniform, so it must be grounded in changes in their specific social and cultural contexts.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: How should a scholar construct a braided literary history of the early modern and nineteenth centuries?
choices: Interweave works around a recurring problem while preserving each work’s distinct historical context
Arrange works chronologically within each period and compare their conclusions
Rank works by their influence on later canonical literary movements
End each period whenever a recurring problem appears in a new form
items.answer: Interweave works around a recurring problem while preserving each work’s distinct historical context
items.rationale: A braided narrative connects works across time through a shared problem without erasing the historical differences that shaped each work.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: Which proposed periodization would best support an alternative literary history based on changes in print technology and reading practices?
choices: Print culture and industrial reading, 1750–1850
Monarchical patronage and court literature, 1680–1800
Romanticism to realism, 1790–1880
National revival and modernist reform, 1880–1930
items.answer: Print culture and industrial reading, 1750–1850
items.rationale: This periodization makes technological and reading practices its organizing principle rather than relying on rulers or conventional literary movements.

source.claim: The rise of industrial printing and changes in reading practices occurred mainly between 1750 and 1850.
source.quote: Technological improvements during the Industrial Revolution in printing and paper production; and new distribution networks enabled by improved roads and rail helped push an increased demand for printed (reading) matter.

items.prompt: Which approach most clearly fulfills the purpose of a state-of-the-field essay?
choices: Critiquing the methods and findings of a single study
Cataloging every article published in one journal
Synthesizing and evaluating scholarship across a broad disciplinary field
Summarizing the arguments of one influential scholar
items.answer: Synthesizing and evaluating scholarship across a broad disciplinary field
items.rationale: It synthesizes and evaluates a whole field, the defining function of a state-of-the-field essay.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: A field’s studies repeatedly use the same flawed dataset. What should the essay emphasize?
choices: The dataset’s publication dates and author names
How the shared flaw limits the field’s collective conclusions
Only the most recent study using that dataset
The dataset developers’ recommendations without weighing evidence
items.answer: How the shared flaw limits the field’s collective conclusions
items.rationale: It identifies a cross-study limitation and explains how it affects the field’s collective conclusions.

items.prompt: Which evidence best supports a judgment that a field has reached theoretical consensus?
choices: The annual number of articles in one leading journal
The field’s textbook chronology and publication history
Citations received by one early, foundational article
Agreement among key arguments across representative scholarship
items.answer: Agreement among key arguments across representative scholarship
items.rationale: Consensus requires convergence across the field, not simple publication or citation counts.

items.prompt: A survey lists many studies but leaves the field’s central disputes unclear. Which revision is strongest?
choices: Arrange studies alphabetically by author without further analysis
Replace peer-reviewed studies with accessible news commentary
Group studies by competing claims and judge their evidence
Add more titles while preserving the flat chronological listing
items.answer: Group studies by competing claims and judge their evidence
items.rationale: A field essay should synthesize competing claims and judge the evidence supporting them.

items.prompt: Which study design provides the strongest basis for claiming that explicit phonics instruction causes better word recognition?
choices: Random assignment with a preregistered, standardized word-reading outcome
Observational comparison using teacher ratings and prior reading scores
Student survey reporting confidence after one phonics lesson
Cross-sectional study linking attendance to reading attainment
items.answer: Random assignment with a preregistered, standardized word-reading outcome
items.rationale: Random assignment reduces confounding, preregistration limits selective reporting, and a standardized outcome directly measures the claimed skill.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: A meta-analysis finds a positive average intervention effect, but effects vary widely across studies. Which conclusion is most defensible?
choices: The intervention helps equally for every learner and setting
The average effect may conceal important differences among learners or settings
The variation proves that the intervention caused no benefit
Only the largest study should determine the intervention’s value
items.answer: The average effect may conceal important differences among learners or settings
items.rationale: An average pooled effect can hide meaningful moderation by learner characteristics, outcome measures, or implementation context, so it should not be treated as universal.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: Two well-designed studies reach opposite conclusions about an intervention’s effect on reading. What should an adjudicator examine first?
choices: Whether differences in participants, measures, and settings explain the conflict
Whether authors used more confident wording in their abstracts
Whether intervention was studied more recently than outcomes were measured
Whether one study received more funding from its developer
items.answer: Whether differences in participants, measures, and settings explain the conflict
items.rationale: Apparent conflicts may reflect different populations, measures, or conditions. Adjudication requires identifying these differences before weighing the competing claims.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: A large preregistered trial reports reading gains with a confidence interval excluding zero, while a prior meta-analysis found tiny benefits. What is the best judgment?
choices: Compare effect sizes, study quality, and population fit before deciding which claim generalizes
Treat the newer trial as decisive because preregistration guarantees external validity
Reject the meta-analysis because individual trials always outweigh pooled evidence
Treat the confidence interval as proof of large, meaningful educational benefit
items.answer: Compare effect sizes, study quality, and population fit before deciding which claim generalizes
items.rationale: Statistical significance does not establish practical importance or broad generalizability. The strongest judgment weighs magnitude, methodological quality, and population fit.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: A scholar studying born‑digital novels applies 'platform affordances' to argue that
choices: The narrative remains unchanged from print editions
Algorithmic recommendation engines co‑author reading paths
Digital formats eliminate materiality concerns
Authorial intent is fully preserved in code
items.answer: Algorithmic recommendation engines co‑author reading paths
items.rationale: Platform affordances highlight how algorithms, interfaces, and networked distribution actively shape reader experience and textual variation.

source.claim: Platform affordances are platform features and constraints that can steer user behavior, including algorithmic reading paths.
source.quote: Recommender systems now rank, sort, filter, and suggest information to users, based on a range of data including user behavior and preferences.

items.prompt: Which research design best fits a global history of books and reading?
choices: Compare texts, reading practices, and institutions across regions without ranking them
Treat all regions as stages in a path toward Western print culture
Organize the study mainly around changes in printing technology
Exclude oral traditions because they do not use bound pages
items.answer: Compare texts, reading practices, and institutions across regions without ranking them
items.rationale: A global book history examines diverse local practices and their connections without treating Western print culture as the universal endpoint. The other approaches impose a hierarchy, narrow the analysis to technology, or arbitrarily exclude textual practices.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: A survey begins with manuscripts, follows print, and ends with e-books, using the same stages worldwide. What is the chief limitation?
choices: It assumes a uniform sequence that hides divergent regional histories
It includes too many technological details about early printing
It gives insufficient attention to individual authors' literary styles
It relies too heavily on recent scholarship about digital media
items.answer: It assumes a uniform sequence that hides divergent regional histories
items.rationale: The progression from manuscript through print to e-book is a teleological model, not a universal historical sequence. A global and digital framework must allow different regions, formats, and reading practices to develop in distinct ways.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: Which research question most directly examines reading as an active social practice in a global and digital age?
choices: How do readers mark, share, and interpret texts across print and digital formats?
When and where were the first bound books produced in each region?
How did printing technologies change the physical dimensions of books?
Which literary genres became dominant as written texts expanded?
items.answer: How do readers mark, share, and interpret texts across print and digital formats?
items.rationale: This question treats reading as an active practice involving interpretation, annotation, and sharing across media. The alternatives focus mainly on production, physical change, or literary classification rather than readers' practices.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: Which criterion is essential when proposing a new computational model of reading development?
choices: It must replicate only behavioral accuracy data.
It must account for both orthographic and phonological processing dynamics.
It must ignore individual differences.
It must be limited to adult skilled readers.
items.answer: It must account for both orthographic and phonological processing dynamics.
items.rationale: A viable computational model needs to capture the dynamic interplay of orthographic and phonological processes that drive reading acquisition, not just static accuracy or a narrow population.

source.claim: Reading development involves interactions between orthographic processing, which concerns written forms, and phonological processing, which concerns spoken sounds.
source.quote: Stage two is the phonological stage where students learn the relationship between the graphemes (letters) and the phonemes (sounds). Stage three is the orthographic stage where students read familiar words more quickly than unfamiliar words, and word length gradually ceases to play a role.

items.prompt: Which formulation makes a reading model genuinely developmental rather than merely descriptive?
choices: It specifies feedback through which earlier decoding changes later linguistic processing over time.
It classifies written words into visual, phonological, and semantic categories.
It reports strong correlations among reading skills for children of different ages.
It assigns brain regions to tasks performed by fluent and developing readers.
items.answer: It specifies feedback through which earlier decoding changes later linguistic processing over time.
items.rationale: A developmental model must explain change over time, including mechanisms that connect earlier processes to later ones. The other options describe classifications, associations, or neural locations without explaining development.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: A new model predicts that decoding improvement increases reading fluency, while increased fluency increases attention to print. Which model is being proposed?
choices: A reciprocal-feedback model with directional effects between decoding and print attention
A stage model in which decoding must be perfect before fluency develops
A lexical model that treats print attention as a consequence of age
A modular model in which decoding and print attention develop independently
items.answer: A reciprocal-feedback model with directional effects between decoding and print attention
items.rationale: The prediction assigns influence in both directions, so it represents reciprocal feedback between two processes. The distractors incorrectly impose sequencing, age-based causation, or independent development.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge

items.prompt: Which study would best test whether a new reading model explains development rather than only average performance?
choices: A longitudinal study testing whether predicted changes precede later changes
A cross-sectional study comparing children from two age groups
A case study describing one skilled and one struggling reader
An accuracy study using familiar words and sentences
items.answer: A longitudinal study testing whether predicted changes precede later changes
items.rationale: Longitudinal evidence can test whether a model’s predicted mechanisms operate in the correct temporal order. Cross-sectional comparisons, case descriptions, and familiar-text accuracy tests do not directly establish developmental change.

verified.source: no factual claim named by either judge
